hints: Identify the radiation’s physical nature and where it originates.
walkthrough: Gamma radiation consists of photons of electromagnetic radiation emitted from nuclei.

hints: Take logarithms to turn the attenuation relation into a straight-line equation.
Use a large triangle on a drawn best-fit line, not individual noisy points.
walkthrough: $\ln C=\ln C_0-\mu x$, so the gradient of a plot of $\ln C$ against $x$ is $-\mu$.
Draw a best-fit straight line and choose widely separated points on it.
Evaluate $\mu=-\Delta(\ln C)/\Delta x$ using $x$ in millimetres. The graph gives approximately $0.061\,\mathrm{mm^{-1}}$.
The coefficient is positive even though the graph slopes downwards.

hints: Compare the fraction absorbed per unit thickness by aluminium and lead.
walkthrough: Aluminium absorbs this gamma radiation less strongly than lead, so count rate falls less rapidly with thickness.
The magnitude of the negative slope of ln C against x is smaller; therefore the attenuation coefficient is smaller.
